{{Quote|This was our castle, our crossroads of technology and talent and you've ripped up the foundations.|[[Rasmus Blys]]|<ref name="Titans" />}}
The '''Seizure of CZ-198''' was a skirmish during [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka]]'s reorganization of [[3638 BBY]]<ref name="date" /> between a rebellious entity within Czerka Corporation and the forces of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the resurgent [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], battling for Czerka assets in an advanced [[Czerka facility (CZ-198)|facility]] on the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] [[CZ-198]] in [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]].

==Prelude==
{{Quote|I built CZ-198 up from nothing. A scrubby storage outpost became our flagship research center because of me. You think you could take it all away?|Rasmus Blys|<ref name="Titans" />}}
At the height of the [[Galactic War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|resurgent Sith Empire]], which caused a shortage of resources for both sides, [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka Corporation]]'s scandalous means of doing business and corrupt corporate culture provided an opportunity for the Republic to nationalize the corporation. Under legal means, Republic's [[Department of Adjudication]], an organization responsible for regulating corporations and the health of the galactic economy, moved to seize the assets of the organization.<ref name="Titans" />

Seeking to stem the loss of his personal wealth, [[Torkel Laphmer]], a Czerka senior executive, negotiated a trade of classified information for a mansion and a lifetime salary with the leader of the seizure, Adjudicator [[Refain]]. Within the secret documents was information about the classified facility on the desolate moon of [[CZ-198]], its contents and a prototype security system called [[Vigilant|"the Vigilant"]]. Identifying the facility as a threat and fearing that his forces would not be enough to quell Czerka opposition, should negotiations fail and the situation became violent, the leader of the Adjudicators called upon the help of various Republic heroes.<ref name="Titans" />

At the same time, some of [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka]] officials lead by the chief operations officer of [[Czerka Weapons Division]], a [[Mirialan/Legends|Mirialan]] [[Eva Kaayz]], turned to the Empire for help. Eva Kaayz approached [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Kresk]] in charge of the [[Imperial Ordnance Acquisition Corps]], an organization created to acquire any and all scientific and technological edge for the defense of the Empire, proposing a mutually beneficial coalition. Promising to give Czerka's technological secrets to the Sith Empire, she revealed to him the contents of the [[CZ-198]] [[Czerka facility (CZ-198)|facility]] as well, suggesting the imperials should take it by force, while the Republic attempts negotiations. To accomplish this, Moff Kresk also called upon various Imperial heroes.<ref name="Titans" />
[[File:CZ_rasmus_stands_ready.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Rasmus stands ready]]
The [[Czerka facility (CZ-198)|facility]] itself, however, was controlled by Special Executive [[Rasmus Blys]], who built it from an insignificant remote warehouse into a state of the art institution for research and production of cutting-edge products.<ref name="codex">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=codex|CZ-198}}</ref> When rumors of the fall of Czerka and its consequent seizure by the Republic reached [[CZ-198]], Rasmus consoled his employees stating that he was working on solutions to prevent the same from happening to his facility. He locked the moon down, activating countless battle droids to defend the facility he deemed his own from invaders coming from both galactic superpowers. Personnel loyal to Blys' cause took key positions to hold the [[Czerka facility (CZ-198)|facility]] through any means.<ref name="Titans" />

==Battle==
[[File:CZ_landing_pad.png|thumb|right|250px|The galactic powers land]]
{{Quote|All the forgotten tech of the galaxy, reforged, perfected in Czerka's hands.|Rasmus Blys|<ref name="Titans" />}}
[[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] and [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Imperial]] forces were able to land and capture opposite sides of the [[CZ-198 Shipping Department]]. Securing their respective landing zones, both galactic powers moved to capture nearby personnel and established supply areas for further incursions deeper into the [[Czerka facility (CZ-198)|facility]].<ref name="location">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=location|[[CZ-198]]}}</ref>

Strike teams of both forces were tasked with eliminating militant and entrenched Czerka personnel and destroying inactivated [[ZX-10 Combat Droid]]s. Imperial forces were additionally tasked with acquiring a new [[biotoxin]] while Republic forces seized an alternative form of [[Kolto/Legends|kolto]], both created in [[Czerka facility (CZ-198)|CZ-198]]. Czerka forces disposed of an [[anti-toxin]] specifically to counteract the biotoxin in the area which was then collected by a strike force from the sewers of the facility. The toxin was guarded by [[Project DS-5]], a tentacled experiment assumed to have been trashed.<ref name="Daily">{{TORcite|exp=rothc|type=weekly|Daily Area: CZ-198|[[CZ-198]]}}</ref>

===To Czerka labs===
{{Quote|My workers understand brand loyalty. This lockdown's just a formality. If they want to leave, all they need to do is ask.|Rasmus Blys|<ref name="labs" />}}
To end the siege of CZ-198 and unseal the establishment, the strike team was sent after [[Rasmus Blys]]. Using the in-facility [[Rocket tram|rail]] system, the team arrived to the main [[Czerka Corporate Labs|offices]]. Mowing down heavy resistance while avoiding fleeing non-combatants, the team moved from the office's reception area to the [[Atrium (CZ-198)|Atrium]] where they searched the abandoned offices for three security cards needed to access the following section of the facility. Through out their advancement, Rasmus Blus was periodically contacting the team through the public address system, attempting to intimidate them or damage their morale. Upon reaching the bottom of the flooded atrium, the team found the way blocked by the an eradicator droid [[CZ-8X Eradicator Droid|CZ-8X]], acquired by Rasmus from [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], which guarded a [[Particle shield/Legends|shielded]] pathway.<ref name="labs" />
[[File:Seario_Memorial_Showroom.png|thumb|left|250px|The Seario Memorial Showroom before the battle]]
Aided by small [[CZ-2X Infiltrator Droid|CZ-2X infiltrator droids]], massive CZ-8X proved to be a formidable challenge, but nevertheless was defeated, despite the water flooding the atrium, which intensified droid's electrifying attacks. With found key cards, the team disabled the shield blocking the pathway, and advanced further, going through the [[Seario Memorial Showroom]] and dispensing of the standard Czerka security resistance. Arriving at the security office, the strike force was stalled by the chief of security, [[Zokar]]. Armed with an array of weaponry from [[CryoBan grenade/Legends|CryoBan grenades]] to a plasma launcher and augmented by a squad of battle droids, Zokar fought to the best of his abilities but was unable to stand against the attacks of the strike team and was killed.<ref name="labs" />

Continuing on toward the facility's labs, the strike force found the personal experiments of the maddened special executive, including mutated [[Flesh Raider]]s of the [[Project TG-5]] and [[Project EK-8|EK-8]], which exploded on contact. Multiple specimens were located through halls the team walked through, each endangering lives as TG-5s blasted anyone who had come close enough with a massive wave of concussive force. Contained with [[cryotank]]s, EK-8s brawled when released but discharged a pheromone that attracted the crimson TG-5s. The team used this to their advantage, surviving the onslaught of concussive force while releasing the blue tinged EK-8s in order to quickly destroy both.<ref name="labs" />

As the strike team entered the door to [[Rasmus Blys|Rasmus]]' lab, they were met with his big booming voice. While demonizing the strike force for destroying the facility and its ideals, Rasmus Blys activated the prototype [[Vigilant]] security system and then engaged the team. Blys struggled to fight the team armed with only a blaster pistol, so he would disappear from their focus using a personal [[Stealth field generator/Legends|stealth generator]] every so often to unleash his personal experiments against his enemies. Using the same tactics as before, the strike team defeated the bevy of EK-8s and TG-5s and recommitted their efforts on the embattled executive. His personal [[Personal energy shield/Legends|shield]] did not hold for long and the mighty Rasmus Blys lay defeated. The strike team approached the command console at the back of the lab and as they began to access the console, a holographic avatar of the Vigilant appeared above it, threatening their demise.<ref name="labs" />

===Czerka meltdown===
[[File:CZ198_Biodome.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The CZ-198 biodome before the battle]]
{{Quote|&hellip;you have no idea what we've accomplished here. The Vigilant Security system is a flawless convergence of technology and strategic intelligence.|Rasmus Blys|<ref name="labs" />}}
Meaning to thwart the [[Vigilant]], the strike team mobilized towards the [[CZ-198 Biodome facility]]. Upon arriving they were greeted by a Czerka Informational Hologram, stating the facility's uses and rationale, mistakenly identifying the members of the team as prospective investors. Suddenly the dome rumbled, doors sealed and artificial lights dimmed. The image of the feminine holoprojection turned into the gruesome, ruby-tinted visage of the Vigilant, a mutated [[Flesh Raider]] who had taken over the once serene facility. In order for the team to progress they had to disable all the information kiosks around the dome.<ref name="core meltdown" />

Fighting through heavy pockets of security droids, the team was able to disable all three kiosks and advanced through the unsealed door towards the facilities energy core. There they once again met with a shut path towards the Vigilant. Upon investigation, they had surmised that the [[Vigilant]]'s rampage had destabilized the nearby biodome's experiments and in order for them to progress safely they needed to suppress its inhabitants run berserk.<ref name="core meltdown" />

Within the desert biome the strike team would find an enhanced [[duneclaw]]. As the team engaged the massive creature, the biome's [[Sandstorm/Legends|sandstorm]] simulation turned on, making the already deadly fight much harder. While retreating, the strike team sighted generators responsible for the sandstorm. The team regrouped near the generators luring the pursuing beast to destroy the dynamos that powered the sandstorm, and with generators destroyed, made quick work of the creature. The humid Jungle biome was guarded by an enhanced [[Vrblther/Legends|vrblther]]. Luring the creature to attack the colonies of poisonous [[Fungus/Legends|fungi]] growing in the biome, which released clouds of hazardous spores weakening the creature, the team was able to defeat it, along with flocks of [[Bogwing/Legends|bogwings]], that ambushed the heroes while they were fighting.<ref name="core meltdown" />

[[File:Vigilant_Integration_Chamber.png|thumb|left|250px|The Vigilant's lair]]
After dealing with the creatures, the team was able to safely use the monitor consoles to shutoff the biomes, which unlocked the doors to the [[Bioweapon Observation Chamber]]. As the team entered they saw the wholesale massacre of [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka]] scientists trapped in the cells once inhabited by [[Flesh Raider]]s they experimented on. Now released, the enhanced Flesh Raiders, grown to become bioweapons, assailed the surprised strike team. The experimental bio weapons did not stand a chance against the strike team, but the lockdown in effect once again impeded their progress. Accessing several consoles around the chamber, the team was able to impair power conduits for the last door to the [[Vigilant Integration Chamber]].<ref name="core meltdown" />

As they walked into the chamber of the [[Vigilant]], the strike team bore witness to the experimental security system's final initialization protocols to be started. Trying to stop this process, the strike team went into action destroying several data integration points around the cylindrical room, whilst engaging numerous groups of mutant [[Flesh Raider]]s summoned by the imprisoned security system. As the strike team destroyed the last point, the Vigilant finished its initialization protocol, charged itself to full power and dove to attack the team. After an intense fight, the team stood victorious over the once ruthless beast.<ref name="core meltdown" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The Republic wants to drain Czerka's lifeblood, the Empire wants us in chains. But what doesn't destroy us, will drive us!|Rasmus Blys|<ref name="Titans" />}}
The seizure of CZ-198 is part of daily single player missions and two 4-player flashpoints in the [[Star Wars video games|MMORPG]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Rise of the Hutt Cartel]]''; released on [[June 8]], [[2013]] as part of Game Update 2.3: ''Titans of Industry''.<ref name="TOR-update">{{TORweb|url=gameupdates/titans_of_industry|text=TITANS OF INDUSTRY}}</ref><ref name="TOR-update2">{{TORweb|url=patchnotes/2.3/titans-industry|text=Game Update 2.3: Titans of Industry Patch Notes}}</ref>

The flashpoints (Flashpoint: Czerka Labs and Flashpoint: Czerka Meltdown) are available to both factions in the game, as such, the victory conditions are not set in canon and thus the aftermath of the battle is limited to secondary observations. If an Imperial player finishes the flashpoint, the Empire captures the facility and takes control of Czerka Corporation, with it an industry that is true to ruthlessness of Imperial ideals. If a Republic player finishes the flashpoint, the Galactic Republic captures the facility, takes control of Czerka Corporation and moves to indict several of its former executives.<ref name="Titans" /> 

Regardless of the faction taking over CZ-198, [[Czerka Arms/Legends|Czerka Corporation]] itself gets reorganized into Czerka Interstellar, with or without Imperial help, to continue existing while avoiding Republic nationalization. In the following expansions of ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', Czerka becomes active as an independent force once again, as seen in the ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Legacy of the Sith|Legacy of the Sith]]''<ref>{{TORcite|exp=lots|type=location|Crash Site|[[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]]}}</ref>
